title: A New Dawn For Mathematical Progress | NOEMA
gist: Atoosa Kasirzadeh argues that frontier AI's recent run of mathematical breakthroughs (formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem, Navier-Stokes, a Clay Millennium problem on October 26) ends the 'checklist model' of progress and its lone-hero reward system, but not human mathematics. She proposes a 'generative encounter model' (exemplified by Dantzig's linear programming and Wiener's cybernetics) and names urgent problems—provably safe cyber infrastructure, a mathematical science of deep learning, multi-agent control, and verifying machine-generated proofs—requiring redesigned credit and institutions.

themes.theme: Checklist model vs generative encounter model

insights.claim: Kasirzadeh distinguishes a checklist model of mathematical progress, which counts solved pre-specified problems, from a generative encounter model in which progress is open-ended and shaped by human purpose.

insights.so_what: A useful lens for any knowledge field: AI commoditizes checklist-style tasks, while problem formulation retains value.

insights.claim: The checklist model underpins both mathematics' prestige economy (Olympiad medals, Fields Medal, Millennium Prizes) and AI's benchmark culture, because it makes progress neat and measurable.
